$comment: The source of sf-resizer's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/resizer (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

min.x-summary: The narrowest width: a CSS length, tokens included

max.x-summary: The widest width: a CSS length, tokens included

step.x-summary: Pixels an arrow key moves; Shift, PageUp and PageDown move four steps

value.x-summary: A width the host keeps for the person, in pixels; it wins over this browser's memory

default.$comment: The handle draws nothing of its own: the host is the separator, its line a ::after of its own sheet. There is no markup to write (§5.1).

accessibility.$comment: The host is a focusable separator (aria-orientation vertical by its role) with aria-valuenow the width in pixels between aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax; its description (title) says how to use it. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight follow the writing direction and the edge.

x-summary: A handle on a panel's edge that changes the panel's width by a drag, the keyboard or a double click back to the default, within limits; optionally remembered in the browser.
x-renamed: events.sf-resize → resize (sf-resizer-resize): the DOM name takes the tag (§8, vocabulary §7)
settings.step: a numeral → number (§16 item 29); value: a width in pixels → number, nullable

forbidden_client_responsibilities: saving the width on a server

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-resizer when a person should widen or narrow a panel, a menu column or a side area by its edge. Put it inside the panel; give min and max; write the width to the variable the panel's stylesheet reads.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not rely on pointer dragging alone; keep the keyboard path
Do not save the width on a server from the component; listen to sf-resize
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <nav style="inline-size: var(--menu-width, 16rem)"><sf-resizer min="13rem" max="24rem" property="--menu-width" storage-key="menu" label="Menu width"></sf-resizer></nav>

x-decisions: number-type: min and max are CSS lengths with tokens (12rem, var(--sf-g3)), resolved in the target's context, so they stay strings; step is a number of pixels from 1; value is a number of pixels, nullable (no width kept).
own-verb-words: resize is a verb of the resizer alone (vocabulary §5 has none for a width); its word is lang events.resize.label. It reports, it does not ask: not cancelable.
version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: sf-resize is a dated alias of sf-resizer-resize, step and value are numbers; a minor while the alias holds (§4.10).

key-effects: role separator; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight step:-1 and step:+1 (step pixels, in the writing direction), PageUp and PageDown step:+page and step:-page (four steps), Home and End to:min and to:max, Enter and Space revert (back to the width the stylesheet gives, forgotten); keyboard.host says the same.

persistence (§7.5): the width is a person's view preference; with storage-key it is kept in this browser through SF.Preferences (persist local, key sf-resizer/<storage-key>) and the host may keep it for the person and hand it back as value; a leaf has no keys, so the manifest keeps it as these two settings.
base: the handle draws nothing, so it stays an HTMLElement: elementFromManifest over a host base that gives the scope (§7.7) and installs aliases.json (§16.20); the Smart renderer would add nothing.

target: the setting is its attribute (a selector of the ancestor to resize); the property target stays the method target() that answers that element, public since 1.0.0, so a page that calls it does not break; the property form waits for the next major.
template: none; the host is the separator and its line is a ::after of its sheet (scss/_smart__resizer.scss).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json plus a remembered width, the inline-start edge and a disabled handle; probe.json drives the keys, the value and the alias.
skeleton: none; the handle has no data of its own: the target's width is the page's first paint, restored after layout.

side-effects: none outside its target: it writes the width (inline-size or the named custom property) on the panel it stands in, which is its job, and marks html[data-sf-resizer-active] while dragging.
css-variables: five public variables read by its own sheet (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).
